strings.name: Zhang Yufei
strings.summary: Zhang Yufei is a leading Chinese butterfly and relay swimmer. Two golds and two silvers in Tokyo, followed by one silver and five bronzes in Paris, brought her Olympic medal total to ten. She also excelled at world and Asian championships. After winning the 2025 National Games 50m and 100m butterfly titles, she won four golds at the 2026 Asian Games, distinct from her six at Hangzhou in 2023.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Olympic and world titles made her an important international representative of contemporary Chinese swimming.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Ten Olympic medals
strings.highlights.h1.text: Tokyo’s two golds and two silvers and Paris’s silver and five bronzes spanned butterfly, freestyle and relays, combining individual and team work.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Born to swimming coaches, began swimming young and developed through Xuzhou, Jiangsu and national-team training.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Continental and world achievements
strings.highlights.h2.text: Won the 100m butterfly world title and six Hangzhou Asian Games golds in 2023, followed by four Asian Games golds in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Four golds at the 2026 Asian Games
strings.timeline.t1.text: Won 50m butterfly and three relay golds, concluding her programme with the women’s medley relay victory.
strings.timeline.t2.title: National Games butterfly double
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won the 50m and 100m titles for Jiangsu, with final times of 25.61 and 56.88 seconds respectively.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Six Paris medals
strings.timeline.t3.text: Won one silver and five bronzes, taking her total Olympic medal count to ten.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Six Hangzhou golds
strings.timeline.t4.text: Won six golds at the delayed Hangzhou 2022 Games held in 2023 and received the women’s MVP award.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First individual world title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won women’s 100m butterfly in Fukuoka, breaking through in individual senior world competition.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Two Tokyo golds in a day
strings.timeline.t6.text: Won 200m butterfly and the 4×200m freestyle relay in a then-world record with teammates; also won two silvers at those Games.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Olympic debut
strings.timeline.t7.text: Finished sixth in 200m butterfly in Rio, gaining experience at a major international event.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First world medals
strings.timeline.t8.text: At seventeen, won 200m butterfly bronze in Kazan and emerged among China’s new butterfly generation.
